Field guide / 03—08

Calculate wall area and openings

Keep gross wall area, doors, windows and still-painted details separate.

Vijeron · Updated 9 October 2026

Measure each wall

In a simple room, add wall widths and multiply by their shared height. If heights differ, calculate each wall separately. Note any walls using a different colour or product rather than combining every surface into one paint order.

Subtract only what remains unpainted

Subtract a door or window if its area will not receive paint. Frames, reveals and trim that will be painted belong in a separate measurement. An early rough estimate may leave small openings in, but that choice should be explicit.

Area is not litres

Net area is only the first step. The number of coats and the selected product's coverage per litre determine the volume estimate. Surface condition and application method can change actual use.

Worked example

A 14 m perimeter × 2.8 m height gives 39.2 m² gross wall area. If an unpainted door is 2.0 m² and windows are 2.5 m², net area is 34.7 m².

Pitfall to avoid

Subtracting the window area but forgetting frames that need paint leaves part of the job out of the estimate.
